title: Residue-field tensor of the affine section-map cokernel vanishes
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a finite morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], $U\subseteq S$ an affine open, and $s\in U$. Set $A=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_S)$, $B=\Gamma(f^{-1}U,\mathcal O_X)$, and let $\varphi:A\to B$ be the section map. Let $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}A$ correspond to $s$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. If $X_s\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ is a closed immersion [def-pc-scheme-fibre] [def-weil-residue-field] [def-weil-closed-immersion], then $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\otimes_A (B/\operatorname{im}\varphi)=0$, where the image is taken as an $A$-submodule.

source.place: Lemma 04DG proof, Nakayama and spreading-out sentences (lines 734-743)

proof.text: The inverse image of U is affine since f is finite. Use IsOpenImmersion.isPullback and IsAffineOpen.SpecMap_appLE_fromSpec to identify the square of the two affine charts as a pullback. The induced fibre square and hU.fromSpec_primeIdealOf transport the closed-immersion hypothesis to the fibre of Spec.map (f.app U). Spec.fiberToSpecResidueFieldIso, which combines the affine pullback and residue-field identifications, transports it to Spec of the scalar map κ(p) → κ(p) ⊗[A] B. The closed-immersion affine criterion gives surjectivity on global sections, and arrowIsoΓSpecOfIsAffine transports this to surjectivity of the scalar ring map.

Let φ be the A-linear scalar map A → B and q the quotient map B → B/range φ. The element 1 belongs to range φ. Every element of κ(p) ⊗[A] B is k ⊗ 1 by scalar-map surjectivity, so q.lTensor κ(p) is zero. This tensor map is surjective by LinearMap.lTensor_surjective and Submodule.mkQ_surjective. Thus every element of κ(p) ⊗[A] (B/range φ) is zero, which gives Subsingleton.

theorem subsingleton_fibreTensor_sectionCokernel
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [IsFinite f]
    (U : S.Opens) (hU : IsAffineOpen U) (s : U)
    (hf : IsClosedImmersion (f.fiberToSpecResidueField s.1)) :
    letI := (f.app U).hom.toAlgebra
    Subsingleton ((hU.primeIdealOf s).asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[Γ(S, U)]
      (Γ(X, f ⁻¹ᵁ U) ⧸ (Algebra.linearMap Γ(S, U) Γ(X, f ⁻¹ᵁ U)).range))
